title: Translate position into value
chapter: Make every digit obey both its jobs
goal: Write a number in terms of its digits so that place value can be used.

scenes.visual: The number 42 as four long ten-rods and two unit cubes. The digits swap; it rebuilds as two rods and four cubes: 24.
scenes.narration: The digit four in forty-two is worth forty, because of where it stands. Swap the digits and the same four is worth only four. A digit's position multiplies its value, and writing that down turns digit puzzles into simple algebra.

scenes.visual: A puzzle card with letters for digits, and a tangle of guesses; then one tidy expression.
scenes.narration: Digit puzzles look like guessing games. But if you write a two-digit number as ten times its first digit plus its second, most of the guessing disappears.

scenes.visual: A two-digit number card "A B" and its reverse "B A". Text: "The reverse is 27 bigger." Question: "What can you say about the digits?"
scenes.narration: A two-digit number is reversed, and the new number is twenty-seven bigger. What can you say about its digits? Pause and write both numbers using place value.

scenes.visual: "A B" unfolds into A rods and B cubes: ten A plus B. "B A" unfolds into B rods and A cubes: ten B plus A.
scenes.narration: Call the tens digit A and the units digit B. The number is ten A plus B. The reverse is ten B plus A.

scenes.visual: Subtracting: nine B minus nine A. Label "nine times the difference of the digits". 27 divided by 9 is 3.
scenes.narration: Subtract. The difference is nine B minus nine A, which is nine times the gap between the digits. Twenty-seven is nine times three. So the units digit is three more than the tens digit.

scenes.visual: The list 14, 25, 36, 47, 58, 69 with their reverses; each gap shows 27.
scenes.narration: That gives fourteen, twenty-five, thirty-six, forty-seven, fifty-eight and sixty-nine. Check one: fifty-two minus twenty-five is twenty-seven.

scenes.visual: Sum instead of difference: ten A plus B added to ten B plus A makes eleven A plus eleven B. Example 47 and 74 make 121.
scenes.narration: Adding a number to its reverse gives eleven A plus eleven B: eleven times the digit sum. Forty-seven plus seventy-four is one hundred and twenty-one, which is eleven times eleven.

scenes.visual: A reminder card: "A is from 1 to 9. B is from 0 to 9."
scenes.narration: Remember that a digit is not just any number. The first digit runs from one to nine, and the others from zero to nine. Those limits often finish a puzzle.

scenes.visual: Lines: "Two-digit number: ten A plus B", "Reverse and subtract: nine times the digit gap", "Reverse and add: eleven times the digit sum".
scenes.narration: Write numbers using place value. Reversing and subtracting gives a multiple of nine. Reversing and adding gives a multiple of eleven. Notebook challenge: a two-digit number is four times the sum of its digits. Find all such numbers.

notebook_exercise: A two-digit number equals 4 times the sum of its digits. Find all such numbers.
